title: SLI synthesis for multi-model routing and cost tradeoffs
author: Marisol Ortega
content:
Summary

This document describes a standardized approach to synthesizing SLIs (service level indicators) across multi-model routing topologies while exposing actionable cost tradeoffs to operators and product stakeholders. It prescribes concrete SLI definitions, dashboard panels and PromQL examples, alert thresholds, synthetic test recipes, and a verification checklist to use during rollout. The guidance is intended for platform owners, runtime operators, and oncall engineers supporting Redwood’s multi-model inference routing (hosted + dedicated + private).

Why this matters

- As routing policies route requests between models (e.g., base, quantized, distilled, fallback), naive SLI definitions lead to noisy signals and poor correlation to customer-visible impact.
- We need dashboards and alerts that surface both operational health (latency, error-rate) and economic health (per-token cost, model-switch frequency) so teams can make tradeoffs during incidents and product rollouts.

Principles

1. Tenant-centric synthesis: compute SLIs using tenant-scoped windows where possible (group by tenant_id) to reveal customer impact.
2. Model-aware aggregation: maintain model-tagged telemetry and compute per-model and cross-model SLIs.
3. Cost-coupled alerts: generate alert signals that combine latency/error SLIs with cost delta to avoid expensive silent degradations.
4. Actionability: each alert must map to a prescriptive runbook step (fallbacks, throttles, routing changes).

SLI and SLO definitions (recommended baseline)

- Request success rate (unit: percentage)
  - SLI: ratio of 2xx responses to total requests, computed tenant-scoped and global.
  - SLO: 99.9% monthly for hosted paid tenants; 99.5% for free-tier.

- Token-generation latency (unit: ms per request)
  - SLI: p50/p95/p99 of model-response-complete time (server-side), computed per-model and tenant-scoped.
  - SLO: p95 < 250ms for low-latency tier; p95 < 600ms for standard.

- Tail generation latency (unit: ms)
  - SLI: p99.9 over rolling 1h window, model-tagged.
  - SLO: p99.9 < 2s for low-latency tier.

- Effective cost per 1k tokens (unit: USD / 1k tokens)
  - SLI: sum(token_cost) / (tokens_generated / 1000) over 24h window, with tags for model_variant and tenant_tier.
  - Operational alert threshold: > 2x baseline cost spike sustained for > 30m.

- Model-switch ratio (unit: percentage)
  - SLI: fraction of requests that were rerouted to a fallback/cheaper model after initial decision.
  - Alert: sustained model-switch rate > 20% for high-traffic tenants — indicates routing instability or upstream quality regressions.

Metrics to instrument (minimum)

- request_count{tenant, model, route}
- request_success{tenant, model, route, status_code}
- response_latency_ms_bucket{tenant, model, route, le}
- tokens_generated_total{tenant, model}
- token_cost_usd_total{tenant, model}
- model_switch_count{tenant, source_model, target_model}
- inference_queue_depth{node_pool, model}
- kv_cache_hit_ratio{tenant, prefix_shard}

Dashboard layout and panel recipes

Recommended dashboard sections (for a single tenant or aggregated):

1) Overview — one-row summary cards
- Current SLO burn rate (historic vs. expected)
- 1h request success rate
- 1h cost per 1k tokens (relative to baseline)
- Current model mix (pie chart)

2) Latency & Errors
- Panel: p50/p95/p99 latency heatmap (by model)
  - PromQL (example):
    - p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, tenant))
- Panel: tail-latency scatter (p99.9 over time)

3) Cost & Economics
- Panel: rolling 24h cost per 1k tokens by model
  - PromQL (example): increase(token_cost_usd_total[24h]) / (increase(tokens_generated_total[24h]) / 1000)
- Panel: cost spike detector (24h window) with alert overlay

4) Routing & Fallbacks
- Panel: model-switch matrix (source -> target), showing counts and percentage of total
  - PromQL: sum(increase(model_switch_count[5m])) by (source_model, target_model)
- Panel: route-level success rate and latency (table)

5) Infrastructure signals
- Panel: inference_queue_depth by node_pool (alert when > configured pool threshold)
- Panel: kv_cache_hit_ratio and eviction rate (important for cold starts)

Alerting rules and thresholds (recommended starting set)

Severity: P1 (page), P2 (pager/DM), P3 (ticket)

- P1: Global request success rate drops below 99.5% for > 3 minutes; OR p99 latency for low-latency tier exceeds 3s for > 2 minutes.
  - Runbook: Emergency model-swap and throttling runbook (see runbook id: /confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation-2026).

- P2: Tenant-specific request success rate < 98% for 15m for a =paid important tenant (scoped by tenant severity tag).
  - Action: Notify tenant-advocate; temporary traffic diversion to dedicated pool; open incident ticket.

- P2-cost: Cost per 1k tokens exceeds 2x baseline for > 30m while success rate is unchanged -> Investigate abnormally expensive model-paths (possible quantization misconfiguration or runaway generation).

- P3: Model-switch ratio > 20% sustained for > 60m for a tenant with > 1k rps -> Investigate routing policy churn or regression in model quality/eval.

Runbook pointers and operator actions

Every alert must include a short-actionable checklist in the alert body. Example P1 checklist:
1) Acknowledge the page and check the "Overview" dashboard snapshot.
2) Identify whether the failure is model-specific (filter by model tag) or global.
3) If model-specific: perform emergency model-swap to the verified fallback model using the platform CLI:
   - rwi-cli routing set --tenant $TENANT --route $ROUTE --model $FALLBACK_MODEL --immediate
4) If global: enable soft-throttling (reject low-priority routes) and escalate to SRE lead.
5) If cost spike observed, enable short-term autoscale cap to prevent runaway instance creation.
6) Record timeline and revert changes after stability confirmed.

Synthetic tests and validation recipes

- Synthetic load: emulate tenant traffic profile including prompt length distribution, streaming vs. non-streaming, and KV cache priming. Use the platform synthetic harness:
  - rwi-test run --profile llm_standard --tenant-sim $TENANT --duration 30m
- Cost regression test: compare cost-per-1k tokens between baseline model and new model variant using a fixed prompt corpus of 1k seed prompts.
  - Steps:
    1. Pin baseline model and run fixed corpus: collect tokens_generated_total and token_cost_usd_total.
    2. Repeat with candidate model variant.
    3. Calculate relative cost and quality deltas.
- Degradation lab: inject artificial kv_cache_miss_rate and confirm that latency and cost panels reflect the expected delta.

Dashboard / alert ownership and escalation

- Primary owner: eng-platform/observability team (pager rotation: observability-pager).
- Secondary owner: serving-runtime oncall.
- Escalation: if P1 persists > 30m with > 5% global SLO burn, escalate to platform lead and product ops.

Rollout checklist for new routing policies

1) Author policy in feature branch and run unit tests for routing DSL.
2) Run synthetic canary (20k requests) using the target tenant profile.
3) Validate cost and latency deltas in the "Canary - SLI synthesis" dashboard for 2h.
4) If metrics show cost <= 1.2x baseline and latency within SLO margins, proceed to gradual ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with 30m holds.
5) If model-switch rate or cost anomaly exceeds thresholds at any hold, abort and rollback immediately.

Operational examples and sample PromQL

- Current cost per 1k tokens (24h):
  increase(token_cost_usd_total[24h]) / (increase(tokens_generated_total[24h]) / 1000)
- Tenant-scoped p95 latency (5m):
  histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(response_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) by (le, tenant))
- Model-switch rate (5m):
  sum(increase(model_switch_count[5m])) by (tenant, source_model, target_model)

Known tradeoffs and caveats

- Aggregation level matters: global SLIs hide small-tenant pain. Always maintain tenant-scoped dashboards for high-traffic and strategic customers.
- Cost metrics lag: token_cost_usd_total is often updated by billing pipelines; rely on short-term cost estimators during incidents, but reconcile with batch billing records.
- Noise vs. sensitivity: tighter alert thresholds increase noise; prefer multi-signal correlation (latency + cost + model-switch) for high-confidence alerts.

Appendix: Example alert template (to paste into Alertmanager)

- Summary: "{{ $labels.tenant }}: p95 latency on {{ $labels.model }} exceeded 600ms"
- Description: |
  Tenant: {{ $labels.tenant }}
  Model: {{ $labels.model }}
  Window: 5m
  Observed p95: {{ $value }}ms
  Recommended actions: check model-queue, increase model replica count, or perform model-swap to fallback.
